prompt:
The diagram shows a semicircle of radius $r$ inside a right-angled triangle. The shorter edges of the triangle are tangents to the semicircle, and have lengths $a$ and $b$. The diameter of the semicircle lies on the hypotenuse of the triangle.

Prove that $$\frac1r=\frac1a+\frac1b.$$
answer: Area of the triangle split from the centre $O$: $\frac12ab=\frac12rb+\frac12ra$; divide by $\frac12abr$.

solutions.title: Areas
solutions.body:
Let $O$ be the centre of the semicircle (on the hypotenuse), $C$ the right-angle vertex, and $P,Q$ the points of tangency on the sides of lengths $a$ and $b$, so $OP=OQ=r$ are perpendicular to the sides. Join $OC$, splitting the triangle into two triangles with bases $a$ and $b$ and heights $r$:
$$\tfrac12ab=\tfrac12rb+\tfrac12ra.$$
Divide by $\tfrac12abr$: $\dfrac1r=\dfrac1a+\dfrac1b$. ∎

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body: Let the vertices be $C$ (right angle), $A$ at the end of the side of length $b$ and $B$ at the end of the side of length $a$; let $Q$ be the tangency point on $CA$. The radius $OQ\perp CA$ and $BC\perp CA$ so $OQ\parallel BC$, and triangles $AOQ$ and $ABC$ are similar: $\dfrac{OQ}{BC}=\dfrac{AQ}{AC}$. Here $OQ=r$, $BC=a$, $AC=b$ and $AQ=b-r$ (because $CQ=r$, as $OQCP$ is a square). So $\dfrac ra=\dfrac{b-r}b$. Hence $rb=ab-ar$; dividing by $abr$: $\dfrac1a=\dfrac1r-\dfrac1b$. ∎

prompt: How many triangles (with non-zero area) are there with each of the three vertices at one of the dots in the diagram?

solutions.title: Subtract collinear triples
solutions.body:
There are $17$ dots (two lines of $9$ sharing the centre dot). Choose any $3$: $\binom{17}3=680$. Triples with zero area are three dots on the same line: $2\binom93=2\cdot84=168$. So $680-168=512$.

**Answer: 512**

solutions.title: Choose two on one line and one on the other
solutions.body: Two dots on the horizontal line ($\binom92=36$ ways) and one dot on the vertical line not on the horizontal ($8$ ways): $288$ triangles. Similarly $288$ with two on the vertical line. Triangles with the centre dot as a vertex and the other two on different lines were counted twice: $8\times8=64$. Total $288+288-64=512$.

prompt:
How many solutions are there to the equation
$$m^4+8n^2+425=n^4+42m^2,$$
where $m$ and $n$ are integers?

The diagram shows a square $PQRS$ with sides of length $2$. The point $T$ is the midpoint of $RS$, and $U$ lies on $QR$ so that $\angle SPT=\angle TPU$.

What is the length of $UR$?

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
Let $F$ be the point on $PU$ with $\angle TFP=90^\circ$. Triangles $PTS$ and $PTF$ are congruent (AAS: common $PT$, equal angles at $P$, right angles at $S$ and $F$), so $TF=TS=1$ and $PF=PS=2$.

Then $TF=TR=1$ and $TU$ is common, so right triangles $TUR$ and $TUF$ are congruent (RHS), giving $\angle RTU=\angle UTF$.

The four angles at $T$ along the line $RS$ add to $180^\circ$: $\angle STP+\angle PTF+\angle FTU+\angle UTR=180^\circ$ with $\angle STP=\angle PTF$ and $\angle FTU=\angle UTR$, so $\angle PTF+\angle FTU=90^\circ$, and $\angle RTU=90^\circ-\angle STP=\angle SPT$.

So triangles $RTU$ and $SPT$ are similar (AA), giving $\dfrac{UR}{RT}=\dfrac{TS}{SP}=\dfrac12$, so $UR=\tfrac12$.

**Answer: $\tfrac12$**

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body: Put $P=(0,0)$, $S=(0,2)$, $R=(2,2)$, $Q=(2,0)$, $T=(1,2)$. Then $\tan\angle SPT=\tfrac12$, so $\tan\angle SPU=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac12}{1-\frac14}=\tfrac43$. The line $PU$ makes angle $\theta$ with $PS$ (vertical) where $\tan\theta=\frac43$, i.e. $x/y=\tfrac43$; at $x=2$, $y=\tfrac32$. So $U=(2,\tfrac32)$ and $UR=2-\tfrac32=\tfrac12$.

prompt:
Solve the pair of simultaneous equations
$$(a+b)(a^2-b^2)=4\quad\text{and}\quad(a-b)(a^2+b^2)=\frac52.$$

solutions.title: Divide the equations
solutions.body:
The first equation is $(a+b)^2(a-b)=4$. Neither side of the equations can have $a=b$ (the left sides would be $0$). Dividing the first by the second:
$$\frac{(a+b)^2}{a^2+b^2}=\frac85,$$
so $5(a+b)^2=8(a^2+b^2)$, i.e. $3a^2-10ab+3b^2=0$, i.e. $(3a-b)(a-3b)=0$. So $b=3a$ or $a=3b$.

- $a=3b$: $(4b)^2\cdot2b=4$ gives $32b^3=4$, $b=\tfrac12$, $a=\tfrac32$.
- $b=3a$: $(4a)^2(-2a)=4$ gives $-32a^3=4$, $a=-\tfrac12$, $b=-\tfrac32$.

Check: $(\tfrac32,\tfrac12)$: $2\cdot2=4$ and $1\cdot\tfrac52=\tfrac52$ ✓. $(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac32)$: $(-2)(-2)=4$, $(1)(\tfrac52)=\tfrac52$ ✓.

**Answer: $(a,b)=(\tfrac32,\tfrac12)$ and $(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac32)$**

prompt:
The diagram shows a $10\times9$ board with seven $2\times1$ tiles already in place.

What is the largest number of additional $2\times1$ tiles that can be placed on the board, so that each tile covers exactly two $1\times1$ cells of the board, and no tiles overlap?

solutions.title: Colouring and two staircases
solutions.body:
Number rows $1$-$9$ from the top and columns $1$-$10$ from the left. The seven tiles are horizontal, the tile in row $r$ ($2\le r\le8$) occupying columns $10-r$ and $11-r$. Colour cell $(r,c)$ grey if $r+c$ is even and white otherwise; every domino covers one grey and one white cell.

The corner cells $X=(1,10)$ (white) and $Y=(9,1)$ (grey) are special: removing them, the free cells split into two parts that touch only through $X$ and $Y$: the upper-left staircase $U$ (row $1$ columns $1$-$9$, and cells $(r,c)$ with $c\le 9-r$ for $2\le r\le8$; $37$ cells) and the lower-right staircase $R$ ($37$ cells). Counting colours: $U$ has $17$ grey and $20$ white cells; $R$ has $17$ white and $20$ grey cells.

Each domino in the final placement is of one of these kinds: inside $U$ ($n_U$ of them), inside $R$ ($n_R$), or covering a corner cell with its neighbour: $X$ with $(1,9)\in U$ ($x_U$), $X$ with $(2,10)\in R$ ($x_R$), $Y$ with $(8,1)\in U$ ($y_U$), $Y$ with $(9,2)\in R$ ($y_R$). Each corner is covered at most once, so $x_U+x_R\le1$ and $y_U+y_R\le1$.

The cell $(1,9)$ is grey and $(9,2)$ is white. Dominoes inside $U$ and the domino $X$-$(1,9)$ each use a different grey cell of $U$, so $n_U+x_U\le17$. Dominoes inside $R$ and the domino $Y$-$(9,2)$ each use a different white cell of $R$, so $n_R+y_R\le17$. Hence the total is
$$n_U+n_R+x_U+x_R+y_U+y_R\le(17-x_U)+(17-y_R)+x_U+x_R+y_U+y_R=34+x_R+y_U\le36.$$

Construction with $36$: use dominoes $Y$-$(8,1)$ and $X$-$(2,10)$. In $U$ minus $(8,1)$ place $17$ dominoes: the vertical domino $(1,1)$-$(2,1)$, horizontal dominoes in row $1$ on columns $2$-$9$ ($4$) and in row $2$ on columns $2$-$7$ ($3$); row $3$: $3$ horizontal dominoes; vertical domino $(4,1)$-$(5,1)$, horizontal dominoes in row $4$ on columns $2$-$5$ ($2$) and in row $5$ on columns $2$-$3$ ($1$); vertical domino $(6,1)$-$(7,1)$ and horizontal domino $(6,2)$-$(6,3)$. That is $1+4+3+3+1+2+1+1+1=17$. Rotating the board by a half-turn (which maps the tile wall and $X,Y$ to themselves) gives the same for $R$. Total $2+17+17=36$.

**Answer: 36**
